concept_gloss.applicability: Nedene bağlı ortaya çıkma çekirdeğiyle sonradan oluşturulmuş, uydurulmuş ve katışıksız olmayan uzantıları birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: Kaynak ile sonuç arasındaki neden bağını ve sonradan üretilmiş olma yönünü korur.

concept_gloss.text: bir şeyden nedenle türeme veya sonradan oluşturulma

concept_map.definition: Belirli söz biriminde bir şeyin başka bir şeyden bir neden aracılığıyla ortaya çıkması. Buna bağlı olarak sonradan oluşturulan söz, uydurulan kitap veya kanıt ve katışıksız sayılmayan dil ya da kişi de kendi biçim ve kalıplarında nitelenir.

facets.statement: Belirli söz biriminde bir şey, başka bir şeyden bir neden aracılığıyla ortaya çıkar.
Sonradan oluşturulan söz bu ortaya çıkma düşüncesinin bir uzantısıdır.
Uydurulmuş kitap ve doğrulanmamış, üretilmiş kanıt aynı niteleme alanındadır.
Katışıksız sayılmayan dil veya kişi için de bu niteleme kullanılır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sonucun başka bir şeyden belirli bir nedenle çıktığı süreçlerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kaynak, neden ve ortaya çıkan sonuç arasındaki bağı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Daha önce bulunmayıp sonradan üretilen bir söz veya benzeri oluşum için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sonradan ortaya çıkarılmış olma özelliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gerçekliği bulunmayan veya doğrulanmamış kitap ve kanıt gibi örneklerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gerçek olmayıp sonradan üretilmiş olma yönünü korur.

error_profile.loses: Ortaya çıkışın neden bağını, sürecini ve sonradan oluşturulmuş ya da uydurulmuş nitelemelerini kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Başka bir şeyden ortaya çıkan son ürünü gösterir.

error_profile.adds: Başka bir kaynaktan türemeyen ve örneksiz başlayan oluşturma türlerini de kapsama ekler.
error_profile.collision: Bir kaynaktan nedenle türeme ile kaynaksız başlatmayı karıştırabilir.
error_profile.preserves: Daha önce bulunmayan bir şeyin ortaya çıkması yönünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal gerçek doğurma olayını değil nedene bağlı ortaya çıkmayı, sonradan oluşturulmayı, uydurulmayı ve katışıksız sayılmamayı anlatır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin başka bir şeyden bir nedenle ortaya çıkmasını çekirdek yapar; sonradan oluşturulmuş söz, uydurulmuş kitap veya kanıt ve katışıksız sayılmayan dil ya da kişi kullanımlarını buna bağlar. Verilen dal bu çekirdek ile uzantıları doğru biçimde toplar.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bir şeyin başka bir şeyden bir nedenle ortaya çıkması
sonradan oluşturulmuş, uydurulmuş veya katışıksız olmayan

lexicalization_scope.note: Nedene bağlı ortaya çıkma yalnız ilgili söz biriminde çekirdektir; sonradan oluşturulmuş, uydurulmuş ve katışıksız olmayan anlamlar kendi biçim ve kalıplarıyla ayrı tutulur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilen dört komşu uydurma, örneksiz başlatma, yararlı sonuç ve genel var etme karşısındaki sınırları açıklar.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalın çekirdeği başka bir şeyden nedenle ortaya çıkmadır ve uydurma yalnız bir uzantıdır; komşu dal gerçeğe aykırı ürün kurmayı doğrudan merkezine alır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal uydurma yanında nedene bağlı ortaya çıkmayı, sonradan oluşturulmayı ve katışıksız olmamayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: türeme veya sonradan üretme / düzmece kurma
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yalan, düzmece anlatı, şiir ve ezgi gibi gerçeğe aykırı biçimde kurulmuş ürünlere yoğunlaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Uydurulmuş bir söz ya da metin iki dalın kesiştiği alandır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda ortaya çıkan şeyin bir kaynağı ve nedeni vardır; komşu dalda yenilik, önceki bir örnek bulunmamasına dayanır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal başka bir şeyden neden yoluyla çıkmayı ve türetilmiş olmayı temel alır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal önceden örneği bulunmayan bir şeyi ilk kez başlatmayı veya yapmayı temel alır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da yeni bir şeyin ortaya çıkması alanında buluşur.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal çıkış ilişkisini ve sonradan üretilmişliği anlatır; komşu dal çıkan şeyin yararlı bir ürün veya kazanç olmasını öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal bir şeyin başka bir şeyden çıkma sürecini ve sonradan oluşturulmuş ürünleri kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal ortaya çıkan yararlı sonucu ve bir şeyin verdiği ürünü öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kaynaktan çıkan sonuç düşüncesi iki dalı birbirine yaklaştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal kaynak ile sonuç arasındaki türeme bağını gerektirir; komşu dal bu bağı şart koşmadan genel var etme ve başlatmayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal başka bir kaynaktan neden aracılığıyla türemeyi şart koşar ve uydurma uzantıları taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal bir şeyi var etmeyi, başlatmayı, bulmayı ve yapıtını ortaya koymayı genel olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Yeni bir varlık veya ürünün ortaya çıkması iki dalın ortak alanıdır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: تولد الشيء عن الشيء حصل عنه (maqayis)؛ عربية مولدة ورجل مولد إذا كان عربيا غير محض (sihah)؛ المولد من الكلام مولدا إذا استحدثوه؛ كتاب مولد أي مفتعل؛ بينة مولدة وليست بمحققة (tahdhib)؛ تولد الشيء من الشيء حصوله عنه بسبب من الأسباب (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların toplu anlatımı nedene bağlı türemeyi merkeze alır; sonradan oluşturulmuş söz, uydurulmuş metin veya kanıt ve katışıksız sayılmayan dil ya da kişi bu çekirdeğin yerleşmiş uzantılarıdır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه تولد الشيء من الشيء إذا حصل عنه بسبب، والمولد من الكلام إذا استحدث، وما كان غير محض أو ناشئا في بيئة معينة مثل عربية مولدة ورجل مولد.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل هنا النسل الآدمي المباشر إلا من جهة القياس العام، ولا الولادة الحسية نفسها.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişiyle aynı yaşta olan kimseyi, başka benzerlik veya arkadaşlık şartı eklemeden karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: İki kişi arasındaki yaş eşitliğini doğrudan ve eksiksiz korur.

concept_map.definition: Başka bir kişiyle aynı yaşta olan kimse; yaş bakımından onun dengi.

facets.statement: İki kişi arasındaki belirleyici bağ aynı yaşta olmalarıdır.
Adın tekil, ikili ve çoğul biçimleri bir veya birden çok yaştaşı gösterebilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yaştaşlık ilişkisinin bir cümle içinde açıkça çözülmesi gerektiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılaştırılan iki kişinin yaş eşitliğini açıkça korur.

error_profile.adds: Yaş eşitliği gerektirmeyen kişisel yakınlık ve birlikte bulunma ilişkisini ekler.
error_profile.collision: Yaştaşlık ile kişisel dostluğu birbirine karıştırır.
error_profile.loses: Aynı yaşta olma şartını bütünüyle kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: İki kişi arasında yakın bir bağ bulunduğu çağrışımını korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel benzerlik veya arkadaşlık değil, özellikle aynı yaşta olma bakımından denk kişiyi gösterir.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir kişiyi başka bir kişinin yaştaşı ve dengi olarak tanımlar; biçimin kökenine ve çoğul kullanımına ilişkin bilgiler de bu çekirdeği değiştirmez. Verilen dal çerçevesi yaş eşitliğini doğru biçimde merkeze alır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın yaştaş anlamıyla sınırlıdır; güç, tür, arkadaşlık veya genel benzerlik gibi ek ölçütler içeri alınmaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; yayımlanan üç komşu yaş eşitliğine arkadaşlık, güç denkliği veya genel benzerlik ekleyen sınırları gösterir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal yaş eşitliğini tek belirleyici sınır yapar; komşu dal aynı yaş çevresine arkadaşlık veya birlikte yetişme bağını da katabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal için aynı yaşta olmak yeterlidir; birlikte büyüme veya arkadaşlık şart değildir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yaş eşitliğinin yanında arkadaşlığı, yakınlığı ve birlikte büyümeyi de çağrıştırabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı yaşta olan iki kişi iki dalın ortak çekirdeğidir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal aynı yaş koşulundan ayrılmaz; komşu dal denkliği güç ve yiğitlik gibi başka karşılaştırma ölçülerine genişletir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal denkliği yalnız yaş ölçüsüne göre kurar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yaş yanında yiğitlik, güç ve dayanıklılık bakımından denk rakibi de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Yaş bakımından denk kişi iki dalın kesiştiği alandır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal denklik ölçüsünü yaş olarak sabitler; komşu dal benzerlik ve denkliği belirli bir ölçüyle sınırlamaz.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal benzerliği yalnız iki kişinin aynı yaşta olmasına bağlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yaş şartı olmadan tür, durum veya başka özelliklerde benzer ve denk olanı gösterir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kişinin başka bir kişiye denk sayılması iki dalı yakınlaştırır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: اللدة نقصانه الواو لأن أصله ولدة (maqayis)؛ لدة الرجل تربه؛ وهما لدان والجمع لدات ولدون (sihah)؛ اللدة مختصة بالترب يقال فلان لدة فلان وتربه (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği aynı yaşta olan denk kişidir; tekil, ikili ve çoğul biçim bilgileri bu yaştaşlık ilişkisini sayı bakımından çeşitlendirir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه اللدة أو لدة الرجل بمعنى تربه ومثيله في السن.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل هنا الولد بمعنى الابن ولا الوالد ولا التولد.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnız kanıtta verilen sabit söyleyişin anlamını karşılar; yalın bir sözcük anlamı olarak kullanılamaz.

error_profile.preserves: Durumun büyüklük ve ağırlık yönüyle şeyin bolluk yönünü birlikte korur.

concept_gloss.text: çok büyük bir durum ya da pek bol bir şey

concept_map.definition: Yalnız belirli bir kalıp söz içinde, çok büyük veya ağır bir durumu ya da çok bol bir şeyi anlatır. Söyleyişin kökeni baskına bağlanır; çok yiyecek ve çok otlak bolluk örnekleridir.

facets.statement: Kalıp söz çok büyük, önemli veya ağır bir durumu anlatır.
Aynı kalıp söz çok bol bir şeyi anlatmak için de kullanılır.
Söyleyişin çıkışı, baskın sırasında yaşanan ağır duruma bağlanır.
Çok yiyecek ve çok otlak, bolluk yönünün açık örnekleridir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıp söz büyük, önemli ve ağır bir olay veya durum için söylendiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Durumun olağanüstü büyüklük ve ağırlık derecesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıp söz yiyecek veya otlak gibi bir şeyin çokluğunu anlatırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir şeyin olağanüstü bolluk derecesini ilgili bağlamda korur.

error_profile.adds: Gerçek bir çocuğun çağrılmadığı sıradan bir olayı anlamın içine ekler.
error_profile.collision: Sabit söyleyişin yerleşmiş anlamını sözcüğü sözcüğüne bir olayla karıştırır.
error_profile.loses: Çok büyük veya ağır durum ile çok bol şey bildiren yerleşmiş anlamı kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Kalıbın sözcük düzeyindeki çağırma ve çocuk görüntüsünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız verilen kalıp sözde geçerlidir; tek başına çocuk adını veya bu kalıp dışında kalan her büyüklük ve bolluk durumunu kapsamaz.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnız sabit bir söyleyiş içinde çok büyük veya ağır bir durumu ve çok bol bir şeyi anlatır; kökeni baskına bağlar, yiyecek ve otlağı bolluk örnekleri olarak verir. Ön çerçevedeki süt örneği yetkili kaynak ifadesinde bulunmadığından tanım bu örneği dışarıda bırakacak biçimde yeniden kurulmalıdır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: çok büyük veya ağır bir durum yahut çok bol bir şey için söylenen kalıp söz

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız verilen sabit söyleyişe bağlıdır; buradaki büyüklük, ağırlık ve bolluk anlamları yalın kök anlamına genellenmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Verilen bütün komşu adayları değerlendirildi; hiçbiri bu sabit söyleyişin büyük olay ve bolluk sınırını doğrudan paylaşmadığından yayımlanacak yararlı bir karşılaştırma bulunmadı.
branches.source_phrase_ar: أمر لا ينادى وليده؛ قيل ذلك لكل أمر عظيم ولكل شيء كثير (sihah)؛ هو أمر لا ينادى وليده؛ أمر جليل شديد؛ أصله في الغارة؛ طعام لا ينادى وليده؛ عشب لا ينادى وليده (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt, sabit söyleyişi büyük veya ağır durum ile bolluk arasında açıklar; çıkışını baskına bağlar ve yiyecek ile otlağı bolluk örnekleri olarak verir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المثل لا ينادى وليده وما فسرته المصادر من أمر عظيم أو شديد، أو شيء كثير، أو غارة تذهل الأم عن ولدها، أو طعام ولبن وعشب كثير لا يحتاج فيه إلى نداء الوليد.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل هنا معنى الوليد المفرد خارج هذا التركيب، ولا كل شدة أو كثرة بلا هذا المثل.

root_profile.summary: Kökün ana alanı doğum çevresinde çocuk, öz ana baba, doğurma olayı ve yeni doğmuş çocuk adlandırmalarını kurar. Bundan nedene bağlı türeme, sonradan oluşturulma, aynı yaşta olma ve büyüklük ya da bolluk bildiren sabit bir söyleyiş gibi yerleşmiş yan dallar gelişir.

text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَٰقٍۢ ۖ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْـًۭٔا كَبِيرًۭا

baseline.text: Yoksulluk korkusuyla çocuklarınızı öldürmeyin. Onlara da size de biz rızık veririz. Onları öldürmek gerçekten büyük bir suçtur.

findings.text: Yoksulluk korkusu, olası bir dar geleceği şimdiki ve geri döndürülemez bir yokluğa çevirir; çocukları öldürmek bu yüzden ağır bir zaman ve ölçü yanılgısıdır.

activation_trace.role: Literal taking of life supplies both the prohibited act and its repeated nominal indictment.
Descendants born from the household identify the lives made disposable by the forecast.
Anticipatory fear supplies the motive but not a warrant for irreversible action.
A hand stripped of wealth gives the feared future its concrete economic pressure.
Apportioned giving counters the zero-sum premise and jointly includes them and you.
Deliberate sin fixes moral agency on the killer rather than excusing it through scarcity.
The great-sin branch classifies the attempted economic remedy as an enormity.

changed_reading.after: The ayah forbids converting an anticipated economic future into present death: fear is not authority, because children and parents are named together under one provisioning agency.
changed_reading.before: The ayah forbids killing children because poverty may result.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled ق ت ل at words 2 and 10 encloses children, feared destitution, shared provision, and the verdict of grave sin in one causal sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: A projected shortage is converted into present lethal action. The provision clause breaks that conversion by placing children and parents together inside an allotment whose source is not the parent's forecast.

activation_trace.role: Waste that strips the hand makes destitution partly a possible product of destructive agency.
Something generated from something else casts offspring as the household's produced future.
Exposing a person to death widens responsibility from the final blow to the chosen economic arrangement.
Apportioned benefit offers a non-destructive relation to what the household does not control.

changed_reading.after: The response is also a self-defeating economy: in trying to preserve present holdings, the parent destroys the household's generated future and produces a more radical loss.
changed_reading.before: Scarcity is an external condition that prompts a terrible response.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The feared إِمْلَاق can itself arise through destructive expenditure, while أَوْلَاد are what has issued from the household.
baseline_models.mechanism: The attempted economy is reflexive. To keep the hand from being emptied, the parent destroys the household's own generated human good and thereby manufactures a deeper dispossession than the one feared.

activation_trace.role: Fear shading into metaphorical knowledge exposes how anxiety can present itself as certainty.
Complete cognitive mastery supplies the image of prematurely settling the future before acting.
Concrete dispossession is the projected outcome that the agent mistakes for a settled fact.

changed_reading.after: Fear is made to function as pseudo-knowledge: a contingent scarcity projection is treated as settled enough to authorize an irreversible act.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: خَشْيَةَ can touch a metaphorical knowledge branch, while ق ت ل also carries an image of mastering a matter completely in knowledge.
baseline_models.mechanism: The agent does not merely feel fear; the agent closes inquiry, treats a contingent poverty forecast as conquered and certain knowledge, and then gives that closure lethal force.

activation_trace.role: The born descendant anchors the threatened child inside a lineage rather than as an abstract expense.
Parents viewed from the act of birth reverse the same root from dependent child to owed caregiver.
Old age supplies the later dependency that answers the child's present dependency.
Nourishment and growth supply the material labor by which the earlier generation sustained the later one.
Repair, rearing, and completion make care a long process rather than a single transfer of food.
Smallness marks the former vulnerability of the adult now commanded to preserve a child.

changed_reading.after: The threatened child belongs to a time-reversing care cycle: today's dependent can stand in tomorrow's caregiving position, so killing also amputates the household's intergenerational future.
changed_reading.before: Children appear only as present dependents whose consumption is feared.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context reverses viewpoint across a lifespan: those now old are parents, and they once nourished and completed the speaker while small. The child threatened in 17:31 is therefore not a one-way consumer but a node in an intergenerational care cycle; killing severs its future return leg.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the parent/old-age and raising/smallness reversals; I infer a reciprocal care circuit whose future leg is cut by killing. A live alternative is that the sequence establishes reciprocal duty without making an economic claim about future care.
structural_cues: 17:23 looks from adult children toward dependent parents, while 17:24 looks backward from the child to the parents who raised that child.
The paired objects in 17:31, them and you, place both generations under the same provisioning subject.

activation_trace.role: The stripped hand connects feared destitution to the packet's immediately preceding management of expenditure.
Apportioned giving names provision as allocation rather than a stock owned absolutely by the parent.
A right owned by its bearer makes some outward transfers fixed claims rather than optional loss.
Scattering money in excess distinguishes destructive dissipation from rightful circulation.
The owning hand localizes the household's limited sphere of economic agency.
A collar binding the limb images hoarding as disabling the hand's distributive function.
Releasing the hand supplies the opposite extreme of spending without restraint.
Exhausted strength supplies the endpoint of total release.
Expansion and abundance move final control of increase beyond the household hand.
Constriction to a small measure acknowledges real volatility without licensing lethal adjustment.

changed_reading.after: The promise sits inside disciplined resource circulation: honor claims, avoid waste, hoarding, and exhaustion, accept variable allotment, and never treat reducing the number of dependents as household budgeting.
changed_reading.before: The provision promise simply reassures the parent that more resources will arrive.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding economic sequence assigns human agency to calibrated circulation: meet fixed claims, do not scatter wealth, do not immobilize the owning hand, and do not release it until exhausted. Expansion and constriction of provision remain variable, but deleting dependents is excluded as a balancing instrument.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fixed rights, dissipation, a bound or fully released hand, exhaustion, and variable provision; I assign human beings the role of measured circulation and reserve control of total allotment to the provisioning subject. A live alternative is that these are adjacent rules without a single resource-governance mechanism.
structural_cues: 17:26-30 forms an ordered corridor from claims on wealth, through waste and two expenditure extremes, to divine expansion and constriction.
17:31 follows that corridor with a prohibition whose stated motive is economic fear.

activation_trace.role: Literal homicide anchors the specific domestic prohibition that the next rule generalizes.
Repeated killing language binds the protected life, the murdered victim, and bounded retaliation into one legal field.
Sanctity, protected claim, and inviolability place the life beyond ordinary household disposal.
A binding entitlement makes the exception to killing juridically constrained rather than emotionally improvised.
Taking charge of an affair identifies the heir's authority as an assigned office.
Delegated capacity and jurisdiction make lethal power explicit but derivative.
Crossing the limit prevents even recognized authority from expanding into excess.

changed_reading.after: The decision is forbidden because the household is not sovereign over life: even explicit retaliatory authority is derived and bounded, while economic fear grants none.
changed_reading.before: The parent makes a morally forbidden decision within an otherwise private household sphere.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following homicide rule places life inside protected sanctity and makes any lethal authority exceptional, derived, and bounded. Even the murdered person's heir receives only limited authority and may not exceed it; parental control therefore cannot become an unbounded private jurisdiction over a child's life.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies protected life and a tightly bounded grant to the victim's heir; I infer that a parent's household position grants no stronger private power over a child. A live alternative is that 17:33 restates homicide law without specifically comparing parental and heir authority.
structural_cues: 17:31's specific ban on killing children is followed in 17:33 by a general ban on killing protected life.
The 17:33 exception, heir, authority, and anti-excess clauses progressively narrow who may act and how far.

activation_trace.role: The recently born and still small child supplies the vulnerable beneficiary anchored in the focus.
A child cut off from a guardian reveals vulnerability as a demand for substitute protection.
Attainment of mature strength gives custodianship a future endpoint centered on the child's agency.
Completion without deficiency requires the custodian to deliver the protected claim intact.
Preserving something condition after condition supplies the temporal discipline of care.
A balance of justice turns resource pressure into accountable measurement.
The scale supplies a concrete instrument for just allocation rather than elimination.

changed_reading.after: The child is a future claimant entrusted to present care; vulnerability calls for preservation through maturity and exact accounting, not removal of the claimant.
changed_reading.before: The child is represented by the fearful parent as an immediate cost.

context_deltas.mechanism: The orphan sequence treats a child cut off from a protector as a future claimant: property is preserved through vulnerability until mature strength, under a maintained covenant and exact accounting. Scarcity therefore activates fiduciary care across time, not elimination of the claimant.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies protected orphan wealth, maturity, maintained obligation, and exact measure; I infer a fiduciary model in which a child's future claim governs present resources. A live alternative is that orphan property and filicide remain separate legal cases linked only by general justice.
structural_cues: 17:34 projects care forward until the vulnerable child reaches mature strength.
17:35 immediately converts economic dealings into full measure and straight weighing.

activation_trace.role: The metaphorical knowledge branch makes the motive's slide from fear into asserted certainty visible.
Disclosure to the knower relocates superior knowledge of inward motives beyond the fearful agent.
Following a trace supplies the procedural image of acting only where evidence gives a track.
Knowledge as disclosed reality marks what the poverty forecast does not yet possess.
The inwardly burning heart locates affective projection among the faculties made answerable.

changed_reading.after: The ayah also indicts the promotion of fear into counterfeit knowledge: an unsupported forecast about future mouths cannot authorize present death.
changed_reading.before: The parent has a frightening economic expectation and responds sinfully.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's fear/knowledge ambiguity is tested by the context: superior knowledge of inward motives belongs to the Lord, and following what lacks knowledge makes the perceiving and inward faculties answerable. The predicted poverty cannot be promoted from fear to evidence sufficient for killing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fear/knowledge polysemy and explicit no-knowledge accountability; I infer that the poverty prediction is an epistemic claim being denied lethal authority. A live alternative is that خَشْيَةَ remains purely affective and 17:36 contributes only an analogy about disciplined judgment.
structural_cues: 17:25 places knowledge of what is within persons with the Lord before the economic sequence begins.
17:36 forbids pursuit without knowledge after the filicide prohibition and names the inward faculty among what will be questioned.

remaining_uncertainties: The reciprocal-care mechanism may describe moral symmetry more securely than future material support.
The fear-to-knowledge reading depends on carrying a metaphorical خ ش ي branch into the syntax of خَشْيَةَ.
The ecological and counter-sovereignty outliers are cross-domain resonances and should remain explicitly exploratory.
strongest_changes: The child shifts from present consumer to participant in an intergenerational care cycle.
Provision shifts from generic reassurance to a disciplined circulation model that excludes killing as household budgeting.
The household loses any presumed private sovereignty over life; even explicit retaliatory authority is derived and bounded.
Scarcity fear is exposed as an unsupported prediction that cannot be promoted into lethal knowledge.
The vulnerable child emerges as a future claimant whose property, maturity, and measure bind present custodians.
summary.what_was_special: The packet made one economic motive refract through time, fiduciary law, bounded authority, and epistemic accountability without dissolving the focus's literal homicide anchor.

activation_trace.role: Dry, shriveled fruit or flesh materializes scarcity fear as loss of moisture and vitality.
A smooth surface stripped of visible trace turns destitution into a materially barren field.
Rain descending as provision supplies the life-bearing reversal to imagined barrenness.
Land missed by rain images the killing itself as making the household miss the life it feared losing.
Literal death keeps the ecological imagery attached to the actual destruction of children.

changed_reading.after: In a contained material resonance, the family answers feared barrenness by making itself barren, while rain-like provision is asserted from beyond its control.
changed_reading.before: The family fears an economically barren future.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it assembles dry fruit or flesh, a stripped surface, rain-provision, and land missed by rain into an ecological tableau. It remains valid as a secondary material activation because every image attaches to a focus word and the literal killing remains intact. Downstream prose should present it as semantic resonance, not as a replacement translation or exclusive interpretation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus alone contains a dry-flesh branch in خ ش ي, a surface stripped of trace in م ل ق, rain as ر ز ق, and land missed by rain in خ ط ء.

activation_trace.role: Taking life is the concrete act through which the household attempts to master its future.
Apportioned giving identifies the authority over future benefit that the parent's calculation presumes to replace.
Inability to penetrate the earth supplies a spatial image of creaturely limits on control.
Unreachable extension toward mountain height blocks the fantasy of comprehensive human reach.
The worshipped or deified authority contains the analogy: household forecasting must not occupy the place of ultimate provision.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the calculation performs a small counter-sovereignty: a bounded human hand claims control over life and provision that the sequence denies it.
changed_reading.before: The parent wrongly calculates that killing will secure the household economy.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads household calculation through the later limits on human reach and the ban on another deity. It remains anchored in the focus's contrast between parental killing and the first-person provisioning claim. Downstream prose should qualify it as a structural sovereignty analogy, not declare that every scarcity-driven killing is a lexical instance of idolatry.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The parent acts on life to control a future that the focus assigns to نحن نرزقهم وإياكم.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Fear of stripped means commits the very severance it predicts.** `خ ش ي:B001/B004` combines dread with shriveling dryness, `م ل ق:B002/B003` being stripped into need and a surface stripped clean, `ر ز ق:B001` allotted gift, and `خ ط ء:B001/B003` missing right like land missed by rain. Children are killed because lack is projected forward, while provision is grammatically reassigned to God. I infer scarcity imagination converts a possible dry future into irreversible present absence. The act reads as a catastrophic temporal mismeasurement.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:100 repeats fear before expenditure but applies it to inexhaustible mercy. This exposed the child's killing here as the most violent form of a general scarcity hallucination.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Fear converts a narrow allotment into a fatal forecast.** Lexical evidence: `م ل ق B002` (being stripped of means into need) in `إِمْلَٰقٍ`, `ق ت ل B001` (putting to death) in doubled `تَقْتُلُوا۟/قَتْلَهُمْ`, and `خ ط ء B001` (missing or passing beyond what is right) in `خِطْـًٔا`. Structural cue: 17:26–30 disciplines spending and explicitly presents provision as alternately expanded and narrowed; 17:33 again protects life, while 17:35 requires exact measure. Assigned role: fear treats present constriction as proof of total future stripping, and killing enacts an irreversible miss beyond the proper limit. Abductive move: the packet supplies fear and the divine counterclaim `نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ`; I infer that a false projection from present scarcity causes the killing. Reading change: the wrong is an epistemic and material overreach: fear mistakes calibrated constraint for a closed future and destroys the very dependents included in provision.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:35 retrospectively exposed the core error: fear had treated a measured present allotment as a total future deficit, so `خِطْـًٔا` is also a catastrophic mismeasurement.

words.gloss_range: additive opening conjunction that links the prohibition into the surrounding decree sequence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the ayah enter as a connected decree, not a loose restart. It carries the provision principle from 17:30 into the child-killing prohibition while the clipped opening gives the command a sharp negative onset.

topics.headline: opening link into decree chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the child-killing ban as one member of the larger decree chain rather than an isolated moral comment.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction coordinates this command with the surrounding sequence of decrees.

topics.headline: prior provision carried forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ban tests the prior claim of divine provision against a concrete domestic fear.
topics.reason: Boundary evidence connects the opening conjunction to 17:30, where provision is already framed as divinely apportioned.

topics.headline: clipped negative onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the short opening syllables make the prohibition arrive abruptly before the heavier killing verb.
topics.reason: The sound row adds a local recitation payoff tied to the immediate prohibitive onset.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing the following jussive verb; not simple descriptive negation
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is the command gate: the action is heard first as forbidden, not merely absent. The same prohibition shape later frames the broader killing ban in 17:33, so the child-specific case anticipates the wider protected-life rule.

topics.headline: prohibitive force before the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the clause is a direct ban on action, not a statement that killing does not happen.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the particle as prohibitive and the following verb as jussive.

topics.headline: later same-surah killing parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this child-focused prohibition is structurally paired with the general killing prohibition in 17:33.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give a concrete same-surah recurrence of the prohibition formula at 17:33.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural jussive killing verb under a prohibition; local sense is physical killing, with broader vitality-loss pressure only as lexical coloring
words.prose: {{ar:تَقْتُلُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:taqtulū}}) gives the addressees grammatical agency under a jussive prohibition. The local object makes physical killing the selected sense, while the broader root field can make the act feel like cutting off life-force and future growth; the Form II variant exposes intensified or repeated killing as a contrast, but the surface bans the act without requiring that intensity. The verb is placed before the fear motive, so the motive is subordinated rather than allowed to excuse the act, and the child-object places the phrase in a marked killing-and-offspring field. The same root later returns as a nominalized verdict in the ayah and the same prohibition formula reappears in 17:33.
words.root_gloss_range: root range around killing, causing death, weakening, or deadening force; this local frame selects the physical killing branch

topics.headline: jussive addressed agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressees are made grammatically responsible for withholding the act.
topics.reason: The verb is second-person plural and jussive under the prohibitive particle.

topics.headline: physical killing with vitality-loss pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can sense the root field as extinguishing life and future potency, while the local object keeps physical killing as the selected meaning.
topics.reason: The direct object and prohibition frame select physical killing; broader weakening or deadening senses survive only as lexical pressure.

topics.headline: variant intensity does not control the surface
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that variant evidence can expose intensified or repeated killing, while the canonical surface bans the act without requiring repetition.
topics.reason: The local surface is Form I; the Form II variant is useful as contrast but does not replace the canonical form.

topics.headline: poverty motive answered by provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 17:31 targets feared future poverty, unlike the present-poverty wording in 6:151, and that provision language directly answers the motive.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete 6:151 contrast and local provision linkage.

topics.headline: children in a marked killing field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the phrase as part of a marked Quranic association between killing and offspring rather than generic violence.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence row ties the killing root to child-related contexts.

topics.headline: verb returns as judged noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same act moving from prevented action to judged category inside the ayah, then into the broader killing rule at 17:33.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply both the internal verb-to-gerund echo and the same-surah recurrence at 17:33.

words.gloss_range: the addressees’ own children or offspring as the direct protected object; plural and possessive with generational reach
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْلَٰدَكُمْ}} ({{tr:awlādakum}}) fixes the children as the direct object of the prohibited act and binds them to the addressees by possession. The broken plural protects a collective class of offspring, while the root field connects this command back to the parent-care decree in 17:23. The object is heard before the poverty motive, so the child’s protected status comes before the fear that might be offered as rationale; the provision principle narrows into this intimate crisis and pairs the wording with the poverty-killing passage in 6:151.
words.root_gloss_range: root range around birth, begetting, offspring, and generated issue; local use centers on children under the addressees’ own relation

topics.headline: possessed direct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the victims are not children in the abstract but the addressees’ own children placed as the direct patient of the ban.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the direct object of the killing verb, and the suffix binds it to the addressees.

topics.headline: collective offspring range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses a generated future being protected, while the local possessive object keeps immediate children central.
topics.reason: The plural and root field support offspring or descendants, but the local object phrase centers the addressees’ own children.

topics.headline: reciprocal generation frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the decree sequence move from honoring parents in 17:23 to protecting children in 17:31 through one generation field.
topics.reason: Same-surah root recurrence links the parent command and the child-protection command.

topics.headline: children as provision-crisis focus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the abstract provision principle narrowed into the intimate crisis of one’s own children and then paired with the 6:151 poverty-killing passage.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect children with provision and the paired poverty passage at 6:151.

words.gloss_range: case-marked fear or apprehension functioning as the motive for the prohibited killing, directed toward destitution
words.prose: {{ar:خَشْيَةَ}} ({{tr:khashyata}}) turns fear into the stated motive, not an independent excuse. It governs destitution as the feared object and points to anticipated collapse, a fear-claim contested by the provision guarantee and by the prior divine knowledge frame. The nominative variant shows how a case change could reparse fear, while the vowel variant leaves the accusative motive role intact. Same-surah evidence shows a broader Surah 17 pattern of resource-loss fear, especially in 17:100, and the breathy opening of the motive phrase softens into apprehension before the harder destitution ending.
words.root_gloss_range: root range around fear, apprehension, and informed dread; local use is an accusative motive phrase naming feared future poverty

topics.headline: fear as causal motive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees economic fear as the named cause of the act, but grammatically subordinate to the prohibition.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as an accusative motive in construct with the destitution term.

topics.headline: anticipated resource-loss fear
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the motive is not panic alone but a calculated future-facing fear that the divine provision claim contests.
topics.reason: The lexical rows distinguish informed apprehension and the boundary row places that fear beside divine knowledge in 17:30.

topics.headline: variant pressure on motive role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the standard accusative makes fear the cause, while variants show the role depends on case rather than mere pronunciation.
topics.reason: The canonical local form is accusative; the nominative variant is apparatus for how the motive could be reparsed, not the governing local parse.

topics.headline: Surah 17 fear-economy network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same fear pattern reappearing in 17:100, where fear of depletion also drives destructive economic behavior.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete same-surah links between fear, killing, spending, and resource loss at 17:100.

topics.headline: breathy motive texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the motive phrase soften into apprehension before the harder destitution ending.
topics.reason: The sound row is tied to the local motive phrase rather than to a free-standing phonetic observation.

words.gloss_range: destitution as the feared object within the construct phrase; an anticipated stripping or depletion, not ordinary lack
words.prose: {{ar:إِمْلَٰقٍۢ}} ({{tr:imlāqin}}) is not a separate circumstance; it is the genitive object inside the fear phrase. The lexical field makes poverty feel like being scraped empty, and the Form IV verbal noun presents a feared transition into destitution. Its rarity and its paired use in 6:151 make the term a focused child-killing poverty marker, immediately answered here by provision language. The final qāf gives the poverty phrase a hard closure before that provision answer begins.
words.root_gloss_range: root range around smoothness, scraping flat, and becoming destitute; local use names feared economic depletion

topics.headline: destitution as feared object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees poverty as the object around which fear is built, not as an independent condition that governs the prohibition.
topics.reason: The word is genitive as the second term of the construct and semantically fills the feared-object role.

topics.headline: scraped-empty destitution image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses destitution as total depletion or being emptied out, not ordinary reduced wealth.
topics.reason: The lexical rows connect the local noun to destitution and the root image of scraping or flattening empty.

topics.headline: near-hapax poverty pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this rare poverty term is concentrated in the child-killing pair with 6:151 and is answered by provision language.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify the paired occurrence at 6:151, the provision answer, and the near-hapax concentration.

topics.headline: hard closure of poverty phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the motive phrase close sharply before the provision answer begins.
topics.reason: The sound row contributes a local phrase-bound recitation payoff.

words.gloss_range: explicit independent first-person plural subject foregrounding the divine provider before the provision verb
words.prose: {{ar:نَّحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}) is retained even though the following verb already marks the subject. That independent slot makes divine agency the hinge of the ayah: the address shifts from what you must not do to who provides. The boundary with 17:30 lets the one described there as knowing provision become the direct speaker here.

topics.headline: explicit provider subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that provision is not impersonal; the provider is explicitly named before the action.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun stands before a verb that already carries first-person plural agreement.

topics.headline: person shift into guarantee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the discourse pivot from addressed human agency to direct divine provision agency.
topics.reason: The rows identify the shift from second-person prohibition to first-person guarantee and tie the speaker to the prior divine description in 17:30.

words.gloss_range: ongoing divine provision with the children attached first as recipients and the supplied goods left open
words.prose: {{ar:نَرْزُقُهُمْ}} ({{tr:narzuquhum}}) answers future-oriented fear with ongoing provision. The supplied goods are not named, so the sustaining act is broad, while the attached object places the children first as recipients before the parents are added. That order reverses the counterpart in 6:151 and turns the provision principle of 17:30 into a direct child-first guarantee.
words.root_gloss_range: root range around provision, sustenance, livelihood, and allotted benefit; local use is direct ongoing provision for named recipients

topics.headline: ongoing open-ended provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees provision as a continuing sustaining act, not a one-time supply of one named commodity.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb and omitted supplied object support ongoing, broadly sustaining provision.

topics.headline: children first as recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the children threatened by fear are named first as recipients of provision.
topics.reason: The object suffix resolves to the children and precedes the later pronoun for the addressees.

topics.headline: provision thread and 6:151 reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 17:31 both continue the provision theology of 17:30 and reverse the beneficiary order of 6:151 for a different poverty situation.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the concrete 17:30 handoff, the 6:151 reversal, and same-surah provision thread.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking the parents as a second beneficiary group under the same provision verb
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the parents to the same provision action without collapsing them into the children. It makes the order audible as two coordinated beneficiaries: them first, then you, with a small pause and nasal echo binding the pair.

topics.headline: coordinated provision beneficiaries
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one provision action shared by two distinct beneficiary groups.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the detached pronoun as another object of the provision verb.

topics.headline: ordered pause and nasal echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the child-first order as separated and emphasized, not blurred into a single object phrase.
topics.reason: The sound and ordering rows attach to the local conjunction between the two beneficiary expressions.

words.gloss_range: detached emphatic second-person plural object, including the addressees as second beneficiaries after the children
words.prose: {{ar:إِيَّاكُمْ}} ({{tr:iyyākum}}) reassures the addressees without moving them ahead of the children. Its detached form gives them independent emphasis as the second object, while the order completes the reversal against 6:151. The emphatic pronoun pattern also recalls the exclusive worship wording in 17:23, linking provision inclusion to the decree sequence.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle opening the closing judgment clause and asserting the whole verdict
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) pivots from provision guarantee to verdict. Its scope runs through the full judgment clause, so the ayah no longer only blocks a fear-driven act; it classifies the act itself as established moral wrong. The asyndetic arrival after the provision sentence makes the four-beat movement clear: ban, motive, guarantee, verdict.

words.gloss_range: verbal noun meaning the killing of them, with the suffix referring back to the children and packaging the act as the judged subject
words.prose: {{ar:قَتْلَهُمْ}} ({{tr:qatlahum}}) recasts the prohibited verb as a noun for judgment. The suffix carries the children from the opening object into the closing verdict, so the judged category remains the killing of them, not an act performed by them. The internal root echo moves from command prevention to moral classification, while 4:92 supplies a broader killing-and-error contrast. The stop-heavy movement from act to verdict makes the transition into the following moral predicate sound abrupt.

Same-surah and boundary rows tie this standing verdict to the provision and knowledge frame around 17:30 and the killing sequence at 17:33.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative predicate classifying the killing as deliberate grave wrong, with variant pressure around error and boundary-crossing
words.prose: {{ar:خِطْـًۭٔا}} ({{tr:khiṭʾan}}) is the predicate that names what the killing is. Its agreement with the following adjective locks the two words into one verdict, while its lexical shape selects deliberate wrongdoing rather than accidental error; the contrast with 4:92 sharpens that intent distinction. The root image of missing the mark remains as concrete pressure under the sin sense, not as a replacement for it. Variant forms test error and line-crossing pressure, but the local predicate remains the standard sin lexeme, made audible by the hamza arrest at the verdict word.

words.gloss_range: accusative indefinite adjective qualifying the sin predicate as grave and great in moral scale
words.prose: {{ar:كَبِيرًۭا}} ({{tr:kabīran}}) is not a free-floating intensifier; it agrees with the sin predicate and closes the ayah as its attached quality. The root’s magnitude field becomes moral gravity here, grading the wrong as major without needing to rank it beyond what the local adjective states. The adjective also joins grave-killing scale language such as 2:217 and Surah 17’s repeated magnitude vocabulary. As the final word, it leaves the listener with scale, and its paired ending with the predicate binds the closing verdict into one cadence.
